subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: A, B, C are three newspapers published from a city. 20% of the population read A, 16% read B, 14% read C, 8% read both A and B, 5% read both A and C, 4% read both B and C and 2% read all the three. Find the percentage of the population who read at least one newspaper.

mark_split.label: Write the seven probabilities from the percentages

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the percentage reading at least one paper — the seven values, the three-event addition formula with its signs, and the answer.
insider_note: The three-event formula has seven terms: add the singles, subtract the pairs, add the triple back. The sign of the last term is where the mark is lost.

steps.label: The seven probabilities
steps.margin_note: First mark. Turn each percentage into a probability. Seven numbers: three singles, three pairs, one triple.

lines.text: Let A, B, C be the events of reading A, B, C.

recall.must_convey: That the seven percentages become P(A) = 0.2, P(B) = 0.16, P(C) = 0.14, the pairs 0.08, 0.05, 0.04 and the triple 0.02.
accept: write the percentages as probabilities point two point one six point one four the pairs point zero eight point zero five point zero four and the triple point zero two
convert all seven percentages to decimals
percentages ni decimals ga rayali, 0.2, 0.16, 0.14, pairs, triple 0.02

steps.why: The addition theorem works with probabilities; percentages become probabilities by dividing by 100 and go back at the end.
common_mistakes: Mixing percentages and decimals in one line.
Reading "5% read both A and C" as P(B ∩ C).

steps.label: Addition theorem, three events
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Singles plus, pairs minus, triple plus. Write it in symbols before any number.

lines.text: P(A ∪ B ∪ C) = P(A) + P(B) + P(C) − P(A ∩ B)
− P(B ∩ C) − P(C ∩ A) + P(A ∩ B ∩ C)

recall.must_convey: That P(A ∪ B ∪ C) = P(A) + P(B) + P(C) − P(A ∩ B) − P(B ∩ C) − P(C ∩ A) + P(A ∩ B ∩ C).
accept: the union of three is the sum of the singles minus the three pairs plus the triple intersection
add the three, subtract the three pairwise intersections, add back all three
P A union B union C equals P A plus P B plus P C minus the pairs plus the triple
moodu add, pairs subtract, triple add cheyyali

steps.why: Adding the singles counts each pair-overlap twice and the triple three times; subtracting the pairs removes the triple entirely, so it is added back once.
common_mistakes: Subtracting the triple instead of adding it.
Leaving out one of the three pair terms.

steps.label: Substitute and convert to %

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives 0.52 − 0.17 = 0.35, so 35% read at least one newspaper.
accept: substituting gives point three five which is thirty five percent
the singles and the triple make 0.52, minus the pairs 0.17, gives 0.35
thirty five percent read at least one
heard_as: point five two minus point one seven

steps.why: The question asks a percentage, so the decimal is multiplied by 100 at the end.
common_mistakes: Answering 0.35 with no conversion to a percentage.
